answers.reasoning: Associativity changes grouping but preserves factor order. No general commutation or substitution of a sum is allowed.
The visual p101 states Jacobian rank loss. A singularity is not a change of labels, arbitrary length change, or global matrix symmetry.
A times zero is zero for every scalar lambda. The zero vector gives no eigendirection and would make every scalar satisfy the equation.
The displayed ordinary event-probability quotient requires nonzero denominator. Since probabilities are nonnegative, P(B)>0.
The posterior distribution of state x given measurement z is P(x|z); P(z|x) is likelihood, P(x) prior, P(z) evidence.
When the expectation exists, continuous mean is integral x*f_X(x) dx; integral f_X is normalization, density peak is neither mean nor modal location, unweighted summing is wrong.
With finite models and equal positive priors, posterior is a common positive multiple of likelihood. Therefore the unique argmax is unchanged.
Slide combines new noisy range readings with prior map information. It does not promise zero error or discard either data and prior together.
Differentiating x1=q gives x1dot=x2; rearranging the stipulated ODE gives x2dot=u-3*x2-2*x1.
Under the stated rooted directed convention, tree edges cannot form a cycle. Root and connections are defining; multiple nodes are permitted.
Actual p118 tree: glass -> fragile -> low, regardless of thickness. Non-glass thin -> low; non-glass thick -> high. Missing observations do not specify a leaf.
Explicit tests and their resulting branches trace why a force is selected. Interpretability is not random output, lack of tests or a universal safety guarantee.
Source distinguishes uninformed BFS from heuristic A*. Efficiency depends on the heuristic/problem; moving away temporarily is possible and BFS does not optimize arbitrary unequal costs.

Resolution completeness is the sufficiently fine discretization notion, for a feasible problem whose solution is representable at that resolution. It is not success on every coarse grid or optimality.
On a feasible instance within its completeness assumptions, success probability tends to one as effort tends to infinity, not a finite-time guarantee or cost-optimality statement.

The lecture explicitly denies a finite-step absolute-shortest-path guarantee for the described GA; it permits quickly finding useful paths via mutations. This is source attribution, not a universal GA theorem.
Actual summary associates probability/statistics with perception, localization and decisions under uncertainty. The alternative applications are category errors.
Zero diagonal is necessary but not sufficient. For example [[0,1],[1,0]] has zero diagonal but is symmetric, not skew; opposite off-diagonal entries must negate.

S_A=[[0,0,0],[0,0,-2],[0,2,0]]. Multiplying S_A R gives [[0,0,0],[0,0,-2],[2,0,0]] /s. R S_A instead yields option o2; S_A alone o3; reverse cross-product sign o4. Nonidentity R makes order observable.

Differentiate RR^T=I and R^TR=I to obtain skew products Rdot R^T and R^T Rdot. From Rdot=S_A R, these are S_A and R^T S_A R=S(R^T omega_A)=S_B, respectively. Thus Rdot=R S_B also. Rdot itself need not be skew, as GAP-Q001 explicitly demonstrates.
